processing: Leaf from trees trained into long vine-like branches is hand-picked, then made as raw pu-erh: pan-fired, rolled and sun-dried.
harvest_season: Picked several times a year: first spring tea, second-flush tea, autumn tea and sometimes winter tea. First spring is the most sought after.
appearance_dry: Dark-green large leaves with some buds, usually pressed or sold loose as maocha.
appearance_liquor: Clear golden yellow, typical of young raw tea.
appearance_wet: Supple olive-green large leaves, typical of the class.
taste_profile: Sellers describe a mild, sweet, smooth cup with a floral aroma; research on tengtiao leaf found sun-dried tea with a fresher aroma and a fuller taste than modern plantation leaf.

brewing.notes: Brew like other young raw tea; its gentler reputation means it can take slightly longer steeps than a sharp cake.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year and season as raw pu-erh usually is, with first spring tea the most sought after. One published list of Yunnan spring maocha prices put it at 150 to 350 yuan per kilo, well below the famous mountains, though such figures date quickly.
description:
Jinggu Tengtiao is raw pu-erh from Jinggu County in Pu'er prefecture, named for how the trees are managed rather than for one village. Tengtiao means vine or rattan, which is what the long, bare, whippy branches come to resemble.

Growers remove side buds and leaves and keep only the shoots at the branch tips, a practice called leaving the tip to grow. The result is few leaves and exposed branches. The method is found across the middle Lancang basin, in Jinggu, Zhenyuan, Yongde and elsewhere.

Sellers describe a mild, sweet, floral cup, and a study of such leaf reported a fresher aroma, a fuller taste and lower total catechins than leaf from modern plantations. Brew it like other young raw tea, and notice how it holds up over several steeps.

Look for the harvest season and how the seller knows the leaf is from trained trees. The look of the tree is the whole claim, so photos of the garden help. Jinggu is also known for its Dabai white-tip tea, a separate thing.
history: One account says tengtiao training probably took shape by the Ming dynasty or earlier and matured under the Qing, though this is an estimate rather than a documented date. Surviving gardens using it cluster along the middle Lancang River, and Xiaojinggu Township is named among the places in Jinggu County where it is found.
